chapters.title: Before I Formed You
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 1

1The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,

2to whom the word of the LORD came in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

3It came also in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.

The Call

4The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

5"Before I formed you in the belly I knew you,
and before you came out of the womb I consecrated you;
I appointed you a prophet to the nations."

6Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I do not know how to speak, for I am a youth."

7But the LORD said to me, "Do not say, 'I am a youth'; for to all to whom I send you, you shall go, and all that I command you, you shall speak.

8Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, declares the LORD."

9Then the LORD put out His hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, "I have put My words in your mouth.

10See, I have appointed you this day over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant."

The Almond Branch and the Boiling Pot

11The word of the LORD came to me, saying, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "I see a branch of an almond tree."

12The LORD said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over My word to do it."

13The word of the LORD came to me a second time, saying, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a boiling pot, tilting from the north."

14Then the LORD said to me, "Out of the north disaster will break loose on all who live in the land.

15For I am about to call all the clans of the kingdoms of the north, declares the LORD; and they will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all its walls all around, and against all the cities of Judah.

16I will speak My judgments against them for all their wickedness, because they have forsaken Me, burned incense to other gods, and bowed down to the works of their own hands.

17But you, gird up your loins; arise, and speak to them all that I command you. Do not be dismayed before them, or I will dismay you before them.

18I Myself have made you today a fortified city, an iron pillar and bronze walls against the whole land: against the kings of Judah, its princes, its priests and the people of the land.

19They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you, declares the LORD, to deliver you."

Notes

  • v1 "one of the priests who were in Anathoth" — Anathoth was one of the towns given to the sons of Aaron the priest (Joshua 21:13, 18), and the place Solomon sent Abiathar the priest: Go to Anathoth, to your fields (1 Kings 2:26). The Greek begins The word of God which came to Jeremiah.

  • v3 "until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month" — the month the city fell: In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month… Nebuzaradan… came to Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8). The book's first verses already name its end.

  • v5 "Before I formed you in the belly I knew you" — yatsar, "formed," the potter's verb, used of the man shaped from dust (Genesis 2:7) and of the servant, who formed me from the womb (Isaiah 49:5). "Consecrated" is hiqdashtikha, "made you holy": set apart before birth. Paul says the same of himself: He who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me by His grace (Galatians 1:15).

  • vv6–8 "I do not know how to speak… I am with you" — the objection Moses made, I am not a man of words (Exodus 4:10), and the same answer: I Myself will be with your mouth (Exodus 4:12); here I am with you to deliver you, said again at the end of the chapter (v19).

  • vv7, 9 "all that I command you, you shall speak… I have put My words in your mouth" — the two halves of the promise of a prophet like Moses: I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him (Deuteronomy 18:18). Isaiah's lips were touched with a coal (Isaiah 6:7); Jeremiah's mouth is touched by the LORD's own hand.

  • v10 "to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant" — four verbs of tearing down and two of building. They come back through the book (18:7, 9; 31:28), and the tearing down comes first.

  • vv11–12 "a branch of an almond tree… I am watching over My word" — shaqed, "almond," and shoqed, "watching," the same three letters. In 31:28 the almond's verb and the verbs of v10 meet: As I watched over them to uproot and to pull down… so I will watch over them to build and to plant.

  • v15 "each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem" — at the fall, all the princes of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate (39:3).

  • vv17–19 "Do not be dismayed before them, or I will dismay you… a fortified city… bronze walls" — al techat… pen achittekha, the same verb twice: the prophet who fears the people is given something worse to fear. The promise is made again in 15:20, I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they will not overcome you.

chapters.title: The Fountain of Living Waters
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 2

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem: Thus says the LORD:
I remember the loyal love of your youth,
your love as a bride,
how you followed Me in the wilderness,
in a land not sown.

3Israel was holy to the LORD,
the firstfruits of His harvest;
all who ate of it were held guilty;
disaster came on them,
declares the LORD.

4Hear the word of the LORD, house of Jacob,
and all the clans of the house of Israel.

5Thus says the LORD:
What wrong did your fathers find in Me,
that they went far from Me,
and went after emptiness and became empty?

6They did not say, "Where is the LORD,
who brought us up from the land of Egypt,
who led us through the wilderness,
through a land of deserts and pits,
through a land of drought and the shadow of death,
through a land that no one passes through,
where no man lives?"

7I brought you into a fruitful land
to eat its fruit and its good things;
but you came in and defiled My land,
and made My inheritance a detestable thing.

8The priests did not say, "Where is the LORD?"
Those who handle the law did not know Me;
the shepherds rebelled against Me;
the prophets prophesied by Baal,
and went after things that do not profit.

9Therefore I will still contend with you, declares the LORD,
and with your sons' sons I will contend.

10Cross over to the coastlands of Kittim and see;
send to Kedar and consider carefully;
see whether there has ever been such a thing.

11Has a nation exchanged its gods,
though they are not gods?
But My people have exchanged their Glory
for what does not profit.

12Be appalled, heavens, at this;
shudder, be utterly desolate,
declares the LORD.

13For My people have committed two evils:
they have forsaken Me,
the fountain of living waters,
to hew out cisterns for themselves,
broken cisterns
that cannot hold water.

14Is Israel a slave?
Is he a servant born in the house?
Why then has he become plunder?

15Young lions have roared against him;
they have raised their voice;
they have made his land a desolation;
his cities are burned,
without inhabitant.

16The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes
have also broken the crown of your head.

17Have you not brought this on yourself
by forsaking the LORD your God
when He led you in the way?

18So now, what are you doing on the road to Egypt,
to drink the waters of the Shihor?
Or what are you doing on the road to Assyria,
to drink the waters of the River?

19Your own evil will discipline you,
and your faithlessness will rebuke you.
Know and see that it is evil and bitter
to forsake the LORD your God;
the fear of Me is not in you,
declares the Lord GOD of hosts.

20For long ago I broke your yoke
and tore off your bonds,
and you said, "I will not transgress";
yet on every high hill
and under every green tree
you lay down as a prostitute.

21Yet I had planted you a choice vine,
wholly of true seed;
how then have you turned against Me
into the wild shoots of a foreign vine?

22Though you wash yourself with lye
and use much soap,
the stain of your iniquity is before Me,
declares the Lord GOD.

23How can you say, "I am not defiled;
I have not gone after the Baals"?
See your way in the valley;
know what you have done:
a swift young camel
running here and there,

24a wild donkey used to the wilderness,
sniffing the wind in her desire.
In her heat who can turn her back?
None who seek her need weary themselves;
in her month they will find her.

25Keep your feet from going bare,
and your throat from thirst.
But you said, "It is hopeless!
No, for I have loved strangers,
and after them I will go."

26As a thief is put to shame when he is caught,
so the house of Israel is put to shame:
they, their kings, their princes,
their priests and their prophets,

27who say to wood, "You are my father,"
and to stone, "You gave birth to us."
For they have turned their backs to Me,
and not their faces;
but in the time of their trouble they say,
"Arise and save us!"

28But where are your gods
that you made for yourself?
Let them arise, if they can save you
in the time of your trouble;
for as many as your cities
are your gods, Judah.

29Why do you contend with Me?
You have all rebelled against Me,
declares the LORD.

30In vain I have struck your sons;
they took no correction;
your own sword has devoured your prophets
like a ravening lion.

31You of this generation, see the word of the LORD!
Have I been a wilderness to Israel,
or a land of thick darkness?
Why do My people say, "We roam free;
we will come to You no more"?

32Can a virgin forget her ornaments,
or a bride her sash?
Yet My people have forgotten Me
days without number.

33How well you direct your way
to seek love!
So you have taught your ways
even to wicked women.

34On your skirts too is found
the lifeblood of the innocent poor;
you did not find them breaking in.
Yet in spite of all these things

35you say, "I am innocent;
surely His anger has turned from me."
I am about to enter into judgment with you
for saying, "I have not sinned."

36Why do you go about so lightly,
changing your way?
You will be put to shame by Egypt
as you were put to shame by Assyria.

37From there too you will come away
with your hands on your head;
for the LORD has rejected those you trust,
and you will not prosper by them.

Notes

  • v2 "the loyal love of your youth… how you followed Me in the wilderness" — chesed, the word for the LORD's own loyal love, here said of Israel's love for Him. The wilderness years, which Numbers tells as years of complaint (The people became complainers, Numbers 11:1), are remembered here as a bride following her husband. The Greek has I remembered the mercy of your youth.

  • v3 "Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest; all who ate of it were held guilty" — ye'shamu, "became guilty," the law of holy things: No outsider shall eat a holy thing (Leviticus 22:10), and one who eats it by mistake must make it good (22:14). Israel is the LORD's portion, and the nations that devoured her answered for it.

  • v5 "went after emptiness and became empty" — hevel, the word Ecclesiastes uses for vanity and the name of Abel (Genesis 4:2). 2 Kings 17:15 says it of the northern kingdom in the same words, They went after emptiness and became empty.

  • v11 "My people have exchanged their Glory for what does not profit" — the verb and noun of Psalm 106:20, said of the golden calf: They exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass. Paul: they exchanged the glory of the immortal God for the likeness of an image (Romans 1:23). "What does not profit" — be-lo yo'il, the things that do not profit of v8.

  • v13 "the fountain of living waters… broken cisterns" — mayim chayyim, "living water," is the law's word for fresh running water (Leviticus 14:5): water that flows by itself, set against water stored by hand in a cistern that cracks. The LORD calls Himself the fountain again in 17:13. Jesus offers the Samaritan woman living water (John 4:10).

  • v18 "the waters of the Shihor… the waters of the River" — Shichor stands beside the Nile in Isaiah 23:3, the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile; the River is the Euphrates. The Greek has Gihon, the name of the river of Eden winding through all the land of Cush (Genesis 2:13).

  • v20 "Long ago I broke your yoke… 'I will not transgress'" — the Hebrew as read: shavarti, "I broke," the LORD's work at the Exodus, I broke the bars of your yoke (Leviticus 26:13), and the read form e'evor, "I will not transgress," Israel's promise. The written form is e'evod, "I will not serve," and the Greek has you broke your yoke… and said, I will not serve You. In Jeremiah a written -ti is often read "you" (limmadti, v33; qarati, 3:4; dibbarti, 3:5; shama'ti, 4:19), so shavarti can be "you broke"; and 5:5 says it of the people in the same words, they have broken the yoke, they have burst the bonds.

  • v21 "a choice vine" — soreq, the vine of Isaiah's song of the vineyard, planted it with choice vines (Isaiah 5:2), which also yielded what it should not.

  • v34 "you did not find them breaking in" — va-machteret, the word of the law: If the thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him (Exodus 22:2). The poor whose blood is on Judah's skirts were no thieves caught in the act. The Greek has not in breakings-in did I find them, but on every oak.

  • v37 "with your hands on your head" — the sign of grief and disgrace: Tamar put her hand on her head and went away, crying out (2 Samuel 13:19).

chapters.title: Return, Faithless Sons
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 3

1If a man sends away his wife,
and she goes from him
and becomes another man's wife,
will he return to her again?
Would not that land be greatly polluted?
But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers;
and would you return to Me?
declares the LORD.

2Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and see:
where have you not been lain with?
By the roads you sat waiting for them
like an Arab in the wilderness.
You have polluted the land
with your prostitution and your wickedness.

3Therefore the showers have been withheld,
and the late rain has not come;
yet you have a prostitute's forehead;
you refuse to be ashamed.

4Have you not just now called to Me,
"My Father, You are the companion of my youth!

5Will He keep His anger forever?
Will He hold on to it to the end?"
This is how you have spoken,
yet you have done all the evil you could.

Faithless Israel and Treacherous Judah

6The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah, "Have you seen what faithless Israel did? She went up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and prostituted herself there.

7I said, 'After she has done all this, she will return to Me'; but she did not return. Her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

8I saw that, though I had sent faithless Israel away and given her a certificate of divorce for all her adulteries, her treacherous sister Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.

9Because her prostitution was so light a thing to her, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.

10Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood, declares the LORD."

11The LORD said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

12Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say:
Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD;
I will not look on you in anger,
for I am loyal, declares the LORD;
I will not keep My anger forever.

13Only acknowledge your iniquity,
that you have rebelled against the LORD your God
and scattered your ways to strangers
under every green tree,
and have not obeyed My voice,
declares the LORD.

14Return, faithless sons, declares the LORD, for I am your husband; I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.

15I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

16And it shall come to pass, when you have multiplied and been fruitful in the land, in those days, declares the LORD, that they will no longer say, 'The ark of the covenant of the LORD.' It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.

17At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD at Jerusalem; and they will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.

18In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.

19I said, 'How I would set you among the sons, and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations!' And I said, 'You will call Me My Father, and will not turn back from following Me.'

20Surely, as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed Me, house of Israel, declares the LORD."

21A voice is heard on the bare heights,
the weeping and pleading of the sons of Israel,
because they have perverted their way;
they have forgotten the LORD their God.

22Return, faithless sons;
I will heal your faithlessness.
"Here we are; we come to You,
for You are the LORD our God.

23Surely the hills are a lie,
the uproar on the mountains;
surely in the LORD our God
is the deliverance of Israel.

24But the Shame has devoured
all that our fathers labored for from our youth:
their flocks and their herds,
their sons and their daughters.

25Let us lie down in our shame,
and let our disgrace cover us;
for we have sinned against the LORD our God,
we and our fathers,
from our youth to this day,
and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."

Notes

  • v1 "will he return to her again?… and would you return to Me?" — the law of Deuteronomy 24:1–4: a man who has sent his wife away with a certificate of divorce may not take her again to be his wife after she has been made unclean, for that is detestable before the LORD. You shall not bring sin on the land. The verse asks the law's question. Ve-shov elai has no mark of a question, and can also be read as a call, yet return to Me, the call the chapter makes three times (vv12, 14, 22). The Greek has the question.

  • v3 "the late rain has not come" — malqosh, the rain the LORD promised, the early rain and the late rain (Deuteronomy 11:14), and said He would withhold if the people served other gods: He will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain (11:16–17).

  • v4 "the companion of my youth" — alluf ne'urai, the words of Proverbs 2:17, the woman who forsakes the companion of her youth. Here the faithless wife still calls the LORD by that name.

  • vv6, 12, 14, 22 "faithless… Return" — meshuvah, "turning away," and shuvah, "return," are one root, shuv: Return, turned-away Israel. The play runs through the chapter, Return, faithless sons (vv14, 22), I will heal your faithlessness (v22), and began at 2:19. Treacherous (bogedah) is from bagad, "betray," the verb of v20.

  • v8 "a certificate of divorce" — sefer keritut, the words of Deuteronomy 24:1. Isaiah asked, Where is your mother's certificate of divorce, with which I sent her away? (Isaiah 50:1). Here it was given, to Israel, the northern kingdom; Judah saw it and did not fear.

  • v10 "did not return to Me with her whole heart" — said in the days of Josiah (v6), the king of whom it is written that there was no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart (2 Kings 23:25), the same verb and the same phrase, with all his heart. The king turned; the people turned in falsehood.

  • v14 "for I am your husband" — ba'alti, from ba'al, "master, husband," the name of the god of 2:8 and 2:23. Hosea has the same play: you will call Me "My husband," and no longer call Me "My Baal" (Hosea 2:16). The Greek has I will be lord over you.

  • vv16–17 "The ark of the covenant of the LORD… will not be made again… the throne of the LORD" — the only place Jeremiah names the ark. It was the seat of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim (1 Samuel 4:4); here the throne is Jerusalem itself.

  • v19 "How I would set you among the sons" — ashitekh, "set you," feminine: the daughter is given a son's place and inheritance, as the daughters of Zelophehad were given a holding as an inheritance among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:7).

  • v24 "the Shame" — ha-boshet, Jeremiah's name for Baal: altars to the Shame, altars to burn incense to Baal (11:13). It is the god that devoured the flocks, the herds and the children.

speech.text: Jeremiah 3

If a man sends away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man's wife, will he return to her again? Would not that land be greatly polluted? But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers; and would you return to Me? declares the LORD.

Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and see: where have you not been lain with? By the roads you sat waiting for them like an Arab in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and the late rain has not come; yet you have a prostitute's forehead; you refuse to be ashamed.
Have you not just now called to Me, "My Father, You are the companion of my youth!
Will He keep His anger forever? Will He hold on to it to the end?" This is how you have spoken, yet you have done all the evil you could.
Faithless Israel and Treacherous Judah
The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah, "Have you seen what faithless Israel did? She went up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and prostituted herself there.
I said, 'After she has done all this, she will return to Me'; but she did not return. Her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
I saw that, though I had sent faithless Israel away and given her a certificate of divorce for all her adulteries, her treacherous sister Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
Because her prostitution was so light a thing to her, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.
Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood, declares the LORD."
The LORD said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say: Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD; I will not look on you in anger, for I am loyal, declares the LORD; I will not keep My anger forever.
Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God and scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree, and have not obeyed My voice, declares the LORD.
Return, faithless sons, declares the LORD, for I am your husband; I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

And it shall come to pass, when you have multiplied and been fruitful in the land, in those days, declares the LORD, that they will no longer say, 'The ark of the covenant of the LORD.' It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.

At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD at Jerusalem; and they will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.

I said, 'How I would set you among the sons, and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations!' And I said, 'You will call Me My Father, and will not turn back from following Me.'
Surely, as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed Me, house of Israel, declares the LORD."
A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and pleading of the sons of Israel, because they have perverted their way; they have forgotten the LORD their God.
Return, faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness. "Here we are; we come to You, for You are the LORD our God.
Surely the hills are a lie, the uproar on the mountains; surely in the LORD our God is the deliverance of Israel.
But the Shame has devoured all that our fathers labored for from our youth: their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us; for we have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our fathers, from our youth to this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."

chapters.title: Wild and Waste
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 4

1If you return, Israel, declares the LORD,
return to Me;
if you put your loathsome things out of My sight,
and do not waver,

2and swear, "As the LORD lives,"
in truth, in justice and in righteousness,
then nations will bless themselves in Him,
and in Him they will glory.

3For thus says the LORD to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem:
Break up your fallow ground,
and do not sow among thorns.

4Circumcise yourselves to the LORD;
remove the foreskins of your hearts,
men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem;
or My wrath will go out like fire
and burn with no one to quench it,
because of the evil of your deeds.

Disaster from the North

5Declare in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem, and say:
Blow the ram's horn in the land!
Cry aloud and say:
"Gather together, and let us go
into the fortified cities!"

6Raise a signal toward Zion;
flee for safety; do not stand still;
for I am bringing disaster from the north,
and great destruction.

7A lion has gone up from his thicket;
a destroyer of nations has set out;
he has gone out from his place
to make your land a desolation;
your cities will be ruins,
without inhabitant.

8For this, put on sackcloth;
lament and wail;
for the fierce anger of the LORD
has not turned back from us.

9And it shall come to pass in that day, declares the LORD, that the courage of the king and the courage of the princes will fail; the priests will be appalled, and the prophets astounded.

10Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Surely You have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, 'You will have peace,' when the sword has reached the throat."

11At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem:
A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness
comes toward the daughter of My people,
not to winnow and not to cleanse;

12a wind too strong for that
comes at My command.
Now I Myself will speak judgments against them.

13He comes up like clouds,
his chariots like the whirlwind;
his horses are swifter than eagles.
Woe to us, for we are ruined!

14Wash your heart from evil, Jerusalem,
so that you may be saved.
How long will your wicked thoughts
lodge within you?

15For a voice declares from Dan,
and proclaims disaster from Mount Ephraim.

16Warn the nations;
proclaim against Jerusalem:
Besiegers are coming from a distant land;
they raise their voice against the cities of Judah.

17Like keepers of a field they surround her,
because she has rebelled against Me,
declares the LORD.

18Your way and your deeds
have brought this on you.
This is your disaster; how bitter it is!
How it reaches your very heart!

19My insides, my insides! I writhe in pain!
The walls of my heart!
My heart is pounding within me;
I cannot keep silent;
for you have heard, my soul,
the sound of the ram's horn,
the alarm of war.

20Disaster on disaster is proclaimed,
for the whole land is devastated;
suddenly my tents are devastated,
my curtains in a moment.

21How long must I see the signal
and hear the sound of the ram's horn?

22For My people are foolish;
they do not know Me;
they are senseless sons;
they have no understanding.
They are wise in doing evil,
but how to do good they do not know.

23I looked at the earth, and it was wild and waste;
and at the heavens, and their light was gone.

24I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking,
and all the hills were swaying.

25I looked, and there was no man,
and all the birds of the heavens had fled.

26I looked, and the fruitful land was a wilderness,
and all its cities were pulled down
before the LORD,
before His fierce anger.

27For thus says the LORD:
The whole land will be a desolation;
yet I will not make a full end.

28For this the earth will mourn,
and the heavens above grow dark,
because I have spoken, I have purposed;
I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.

29At the noise of horseman and archer
every city flees;
they go into the thickets
and climb among the rocks;
every city is forsaken,
and no man lives in them.

30As for you, devastated one, what will you do?
Though you dress in scarlet,
though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold,
though you enlarge your eyes with paint,
in vain you make yourself beautiful.
Your lovers despise you;
they seek your life.

31For I heard a cry as of a woman in labor,
anguish as of one bearing her first child,
the cry of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath,
stretching out her hands:
"Woe is me! My soul faints
before murderers."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "then nations will bless themselves in Him" — ve-hitbarekhu, the form of the verb in the promise to Abraham, In your seed all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves (Genesis 22:18). Israel's return is the way the blessing reaches the nations.

  • vv3–4 "Break up your fallow ground… remove the foreskins of your hearts" — niru lakhem nir, the words of Hosea 10:12, Break up your fallow ground; it is time to seek the LORD; and the command of Deuteronomy 10:16, Circumcise, then, the foreskin of your heart. Paul: circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter (Romans 2:29).

  • v10 "Surely You have utterly deceived this people… saying, 'You will have peace'" — hashe hishe'ta, the verb doubled. The peace is the message of the prophets who speak in the LORD's name, Peace, peace, when there is no peace (6:14), and Jeremiah lays it before the LORD as a charge. The Greek also has I said.

  • vv23–26 "I looked at the earth, and it was wild and waste" — tohu va-vohu, the words of Genesis 1:2, the earth was wild and waste, found together elsewhere only in Isaiah 34:11, the line of the wild and the stones of the waste. Then the creation of Genesis 1 runs backward: the light of the first day is gone, there is no man (the sixth day), the birds have fled (the fifth), and the fruitful land is a wilderness (the third). Four times the prophet says I looked.

  • v27 "yet I will not make a full end" — ve-khalah lo e'eseh. The same limit is set twice more in the next chapter, do not make a full end (5:10) and I will not make a full end of you (5:18).

  • v30 "though you enlarge your eyes with paint" — puk, the eye paint of Jezebel, who painted her eyes and adorned her head and looked down from the window (2 Kings 9:30) as her killer arrived. Jerusalem dresses for lovers who now want her life.

  • v31 "as of one bearing her first child" — at the end of Isaiah, Zion gave birth before she was in labor (Isaiah 66:7). Here the daughter of Zion is in labor, and what comes is the murderers.
